newsitem.title: FRANCE: Transport strikes dog several French cities.
newsitem.headline: Transport strikes dog several French cities.

text.p: Strikes by public transport drivers demanding shorter working hours and early retirement disrupted services in several French provincial cities for the seventh consecutive day on Wednesday.
The protests halted or disrupted buses, trams or underground railways in Marseille, Lille, Nice, Toulon, Cannes, Sete, Le Mans and several other cities.
In Toulouse, where the strike began three weeks ago, and in Marseille, transport authorities hired private buses to replace services affected by strikers.

"This is totally illegal," Toulouse mayor Dominique Baudis told France-Inter radio. "Some 100 to 150 people are blocking the company, they have put buses across the street and punctured tyres. Most people in the company want to work."

In Marseille, a little over half of normal services were running on the metro underground. In Clermont-Ferrand, the road transport authority said some 15 percent of busses which were not in depots at the beginning of the conflict were running.
In Dijon, bus services restarted after the transport authority appealed to the courts against strikers blocking depots.
The striking drivers want a working week of 35 hours instead of 39 with no loss of pay and retirement at 55 instead of 60.
The stoppages, which began with a one-day protest in about 20 major cities last Thursday, have spared Paris where drivers are already entitled to retire at 55.

The government bowed to truckers' demands for retirement at 55 after they blocked roads late last year. But it opposes extending the concession, saying it could bankrupt the pension system when post-war baby boomers start swelling the ranks of pensioners from 2005.
